market.summary: The KLCI fell 1.26% to 1,630.36, its lowest close in three months, giving back all of Wednesday's bounce. It broke the 1,640 support analysts had flagged this morning and closed just above the next one at 1,630 (intraday low 1,630.10). Falling stocks outnumbered rising ones 750 to 342, foreign funds kept selling, and Malaysia's factory PMI slipped to 49.9. The index is below its 10-month average (1,694.9) and the 5-month average is below the 10-month, so the market check fails: no buying. RSI 28 is oversold, so a bounce is possible, but the rule needs a close back above about 1,695 first.

catalysts.title: CRESS green-power deals for data centres — more to follow
catalysts.when: First deal signed 28 Sep; more expected over Q4 2026
catalysts.theme: Solar / green power for data centres
catalysts.detail: A JV of SD Guthrie (33.5%), Gamuda (33%) and Gentari (33.5%) signed a 21-year CRESS term sheet with a US tech company for at least 680MW of solar plus 4-hour battery storage in Perak, worth over RM10bn of revenue, running from 2029. It confirms the 30% green-power rule is turning into real contracts. HLIB expects Solarvest and Samaiden to sign their first CRESS projects within three months. RHB (22 Sep) says several developers are in the final stages of signing and expects Solarvest to win 300–500MW by end-2026; projects must be commissioned by end-2028. The installers have already run and are now pulling back; the supply chain (cables, switchgear, substations) has not moved as much.

catalysts.title: KLCI breaks 1,640 support; factory PMI slips below 50
catalysts.detail: The KLCI fell 20.81 points (1.26%) to 1,630.36, a 3-month low, with decliners beating gainers 750 to 342 and turnover down to RM2.7bn. IPPFA's Sedek Jantan blamed weaker domestic manufacturing (S&P Global Malaysia PMI 49.9 in September from 50.2) and continued foreign selling, with local institutions providing some support. Banks and plantations (KLK −78 sen) led the fall; chip stocks MPI and ViTrox rose.
beneficiaries: Negative for: banks, plantations, index heavyweights
